title: Greenhollow — Civic Trust Under Pressure

setting.incident: A severe storm damages the north road crossing shortly before the reeve election.

actors.objective: Exploit uncertainty and institutional delay to weaken public trust and gain influence over the rebuilding process.
actors.methods: Narrative-level influence and conflicting public claims only; no operational playbook.

claims.claim: Iven Brook caused the north road crossing damage.
Lantern claims to know who is responsible for the crossing damage.

evidence.description: The north road crossing is visibly damaged after the severe storm.
The reviewed record contains no evidence sufficient to attribute responsibility for the crossing damage to Iven.
doesNotEstablish: the identity of whoever caused the damage
that no other evidence could ever exist

findings.scope: The available fictional scenario record does not establish that Iven caused the crossing damage.
limitations: This finding does not identify who caused the damage.
This finding does not assert that no further evidence could ever be found.
This finding applies only to this authored scenario record.

timeline.description: The north road crossing is found damaged after a severe storm.
Conflicting public claims circulate and one names Iven Brook as responsible.
timeline.attribution: claim-source-recorded; claim is not treated as fact

timeline.description: Lantern publicly claims to know who is responsible and urges residents to accept the accusation.
Officials preserve observations, interview witnesses and record the crossing condition without presuming guilt.
The allegation against Iven is reviewed; the available record does not establish responsibility.
The public record distinguishes the original observation from the unsupported accusation and records the review outcome.
The assembly hears residents on crossing repairs, public communication and oversight of emergency decisions.

playerChoices: offer practical aid to residents affected by the crossing damage
report observations while preserving the difference between observation and rumor
challenge the unsupported accusation without disclosing private identity
attend the civic hearing and question the repair plan
participate in the election if eligible, or abstain without penalty
implementationBoundary: This is a deterministic authored narrative fixture for cross-domain validation. It does not run a live investigation, court, election, civic simulation, campaign-ad delivery system or persistent player ballot.

proposals.title: Assess and, if cleared, establish a temporary accessible route
proposals.civicPurpose: Restore practical access while the damaged crossing remains unavailable

resourceRequirements.description: Qualified local works crew and inspection time
resourceRequirements.authority: City coordinates; provider availability not modelled

resourceRequirements.description: Temporary route materials selected after site assessment
resourceRequirements.authority: Economy owns procurement transactions; material suitability is not decided here

resourceRequirements.description: Route stability, slope, drainage, clearance and accessibility

proposals.authorization: No construction or expenditure authorized by this hearing fixture

proposals.title: Develop a permanent crossing reconstruction plan

resourceRequirements.description: Compare feasible structural and terrain options
resourceRequirements.authority: Physics owns physical modelling; City owns civic requirements

resourceRequirements.description: Identify qualified design, craft and construction capacity
resourceRequirements.authority: City records civic capability requirements; provider execution is outside this fixture

resourceRequirements.description: Prepare a transparent estimate and procurement plan
resourceRequirements.authority: Economy owns accounts, currency, budgets and transactions

proposals.authorization: Planning study only; no procurement, contract, construction or payment authorized

notAuthorized: assignment of blame for the storm damage
waiver of accessibility or safety review
permittedActions: publish the alternatives and their unresolved assumptions
request physical safety and accessibility assessment from the appropriate domain authority
prepare a transparent resource and funding estimate for later public review
return to the assembly before any construction or expenditure authorization

oversightObligations.obligation: Publish proposal assumptions, known unknowns, and the distinction between planning and authorization
oversightObligations.evidenceExpected: dated public meeting record and versioned proposal summary

oversightObligations.trigger: before any temporary route is opened
oversightObligations.obligation: Review the physical safety and accessibility assessment without treating a civic vote as a substitute for technical clearance
oversightObligations.evidenceExpected: attributed review record with scope, methods and limitations

oversightObligations.trigger: before any procurement or expenditure vote
oversightObligations.obligation: Publish the resource estimate and refer all account, budget and transaction handling to Economy
oversightObligations.evidenceExpected: public estimate and Economy-owned financial record when such a system is integrated

oversightObligations.obligation: Hear affected residents, record dissent and conflicts of interest, and issue a reasoned decision
oversightObligations.evidenceExpected: attributed submissions, disclosed conflicts, meeting record and scoped decision

residentImpacts.affectedGroup: households relying on the north road
residentImpacts.concern: longer or disrupted journeys while the crossing is unavailable
residentImpacts.followUp: record access needs and travel constraints before selecting a route

residentImpacts.affectedGroup: residents with mobility or accessibility needs
residentImpacts.concern: a nominal detour may not be a usable detour
residentImpacts.followUp: include accessibility review and affected-resident submissions

residentImpacts.concern: delays and reduced access may interrupt ordinary commerce
residentImpacts.followUp: record reported disruption; Economy owns any transaction or financial-impact model
obtain service access requirements before route approval

dimensions.expectedSignal: clear publication of assumptions and authorization limits
affected residents can submit concerns and receive a recorded response
no blame assignment without evidence and no exclusion of affected groups
dimensions.evidenceRequired: scoped decisions, review provenance and participation record

dimensions.expectedSignal: technical clearance precedes opening and resource commitments
dimensions.evidenceRequired: independent safety review and Economy-owned financial evidence

limitations: Trust is not inferred from attendance, voting behavior or personal political beliefs.
No resident-level profile or individual trust score is created.
The fixture defines observable civic signals, not a validated social-science measurement.
